cards.explanation: The order is to gather up their belongings from the land. "Gather up your belongings from this land, you who live under siege." (Jeremiah 10:17) Nobody is told to fight or to build. They're told to pack. I think that's a lot to take in when you're living under siege.

The answer is True, and the word is SLING. The LORD says, "Behold, at this time I will sling out the inhabitants of the land…" (Jeremiah 10:18) That's not a gentle walk to the door, friends. It's a word with some force behind it.
The word is captured. The LORD says He'll "…bring distress upon them so that they may be captured." (Jeremiah 10:18) It's a hard line, and I won't dress it up. The text just says it plainly.

The passage says it is my sickness and I must bear it. After the cry of woe, the speaker says, "This is truly my sickness, and I must bear it." (Jeremiah 10:19) No blaming, no dodging. I think that's a heavy thing to say out loud.

The answer is False. The sons are not around. The text says, "My sons have departed from me and are no more. I have no one left to pitch my tent or set up my curtains." (Jeremiah 10:20) A tent with no one left to raise it. I think this is a heavy one.

The word is flock. "…they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered." (Jeremiah 10:21) The shepherds don't seek the LORD, and the flock they were supposed to look after is scattered. That's a shepherd's worst day.

The commotion comes from the land to the north. The text says, "Listen! The sound of a report is coming—a great commotion from the land to the north." (Jeremiah 10:22) North is the direction, friends.

The answer is False. There's no thriving here. The commotion "…will make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt for jackals." (Jeremiah 10:22) Desolation is the word. Jackals are the ones who haunt those cities.

The answer is True, and it's a big one. The speaker says to the LORD, "I know, O LORD, that a man’s way is not his own; no one who walks directs his own steps." (Jeremiah 10:23) That's a humble thing to say out loud.

The prayer asks for correction only with justice and not in anger. It says, "Correct me, O LORD, but only with justice—not in Your anger…" (Jeremiah 10:24) Asking for correction is brave, friends. I'd be hiding behind the oven.

The word is nothing. The prayer says, "Correct me, O LORD, but only with justice—not in Your anger, or You will bring me to nothing." (Jeremiah 10:24) The prayer asks for correction with justice, and nothing is where anger would lead. I think that's a careful way to ask.
The word is wrath. The prayer says, "Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You…" (Jeremiah 10:25) It's a heavy line, and the text doesn't soften it.

The reason is that they devoured God's people. The prayer gives it this way: "For they have devoured Jacob; they have consumed him and finished him off; they have devastated his homeland." (Jeremiah 10:25) Devoured Jacob, friends. Jacob here stands for God's people. It's a heavy ending, and the text gives it straight.
